subject: Arcadia renewal: surge hedge, commit consolidation & capacity uplift
messages:
From: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@arcadia.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal planning + potential capacity uplift

Irene,

Hope you had a good week. Our current term with Redwood ends Oct 31 and execs want a single renewal conversation that covers: price stability for 12 months, headroom for a Q4 marketing push (estimated +30% peak), and an option to expand committed capacity mid-term.

Two asks from procurement up front: can we get a temporary price hold on current rates for 90 days while we finalize forecasts, and can Redwood provide a small drawdown credit if we underutilize after committing to an uplift?

Can we schedule a 30-minute call next week? I attached a rough forecast.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Jacobs
Director of Cloud Ops, Arcadia Health
Procurement: procurement@arcadia.ai

Attachment: Q3-Q4_forecast_v1.csv (csv)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@arcadia.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-02T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + potential capacity uplift

Hi Ben — thanks for the clear ask and the forecast. Happy to run a joint renewal + uplift session. Proposed approach: 

- 30-min call to align requirements (volume bands, burst tolerance, contract cadence)
- We can offer a 90-day price hold on the current list for any signed amendment that commits to a minimum blended commit (we'll detail the bands on the call)
- For underutilization risk: propose a drawdown credit schedule (partial offset for first two quarters after uplift) — sample in attached spreadsheet
- If you want the option to expand mid-term, we can include an 'expand-and-lock' clause: you declare intent and we reserve burst buffer for 60 days at agreed uplifted rates.

I attached a draft term worksheet (Arcadia_renewal_terms_v3.xlsx) and a mutual action plan (MAP_Arcadia_v1.pdf) to get ahead of procurement needs. 

I can do Tue 7/5 10am PT or Wed 7/6 2pm PT — what works?

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Arcadia_renewal_terms_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP_Arcadia_v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@arcadia.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@arcadia.ai>
Date: 2028-07-06T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + potential capacity uplift

Irene — thanks, Wed 7/6 2pm PT works for the team. A couple of clarifying points procurement flagged after looking at the worksheet: 

1) Drawdown credit: they want the first-quarter protection to be higher (60% offset on the first quarter rather than the 25% in your draft). Can Redwood accommodate that as a one-time concession?
2) Price hold semantics: procurement wants the 90-day hold to apply not only to list rates but to any announced model-profile uplifts that would otherwise change per-token pricing for our baseline model. Is that feasible or would that require a separate locked-model addendum?
3) Mid-term expansion: the legal team asked whether reserved burst buffer can be converted to committed capacity (and if so, how consumption is back-billed). They'd prefer an approach that gives them conversion credits rather than a cliff true-up.

I'll bring them on the call. Also including a short procurement checklist as a PDF in case it helps.

-Ben

Attachment: Arcadia_procurement_checklist.pdf (pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@arcadia.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-13T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + potential capacity uplift

Ben — great meeting today, appreciate procurement and legal joining. Recap and next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Recap (agreement in principle):
- 90-day price hold confirmed and will apply to baseline model families used today (we'll enumerate model ids in the addendum).
- Drawdown credit schedule updated to: 60% offset on Q1 underutilization (applies once for the first quarter after uplift), 30% offset on Q2; no credits thereafter.
- Reserved burst buffer can convert to committed capacity within a 45-day conversion window; conversion is treated as an amendment with pro-rated conversion credit equal to 50% of unused reserved capacity at conversion time (reduces true-up).
- For the uplift, Redwood will provision a temporary burst pool for the Q4 marketing window. If sustained uplift >40% for two consecutive months, automatic recommendation to convert to a new committed band (ops will notify).

Action items:
1) Redwood (Irene + Karthik): draft amendment with the enumerated model ids, drawdown credit table, and conversion credit mechanics — deliver by 2028-07-17 EOD.
2) Arcadia (Ben + Procurement): provide final forecast by 2028-07-15 for sizing the burst pool.
3) Legal / commercial to review the draft amendment; we will aim to have redlines back by 2028-07-24.

I've attached the updated worksheet with the 60% Q1 credit and the conversion examples. Once commercial signs off we'll put the amendment into DocuSign (link below).

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/transaction/ABC-DEF-12345
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

If that captures it, I'll route the amendment for signature once we receive the forecast.

Thanks — Irene
